US rail traffic hits intermodal record as October freight gains signal economic resilience, says AAR
candidates.excerpt: U.S. railroads set an intermodal traffic record in October as shipments rose across much of the freight economy, evidence of resilient demand despite inflation, higher interest rates and weak consumer confidence. Intermodal volume rose 9.6% from a year earlier, with railroads handling an average of more than 298,000 containers and trailers per week — the highest weekly average for any month on record, according to the Association of American Railroads. Total carloads increased 3.4%, their strongest percentage gain in eight months, while carloads excluding coal climbed 4.5%. Fifteen of the 20 carload categories tracked by the AAR posted year-over-year increases in October, and 16 were higher through the first 10 months of 2026. The association said that breadth pointed to underlying industrial strength rather than simply a shift of freight from highways to rail. candidates.title: Wheeling & Lake Erie engineers, conductors strike over managers filling crew positions
candidates.excerpt: About 140 engineers and conductors at the Wheeling & Lake Erie Railway went on strike Wednesday, Nov. 11, over the railroad’s use of managers to perform conductors’ work, according to the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen. The union said picket lines went up at railroad locations beginning at noon Wednesday but offered no details. It contends that the railroad’s actions violate both its collective bargaining agreement and a federal court order dating to 2013. The dispute involves a regional freight railroad operating over 840 miles of track, with a network extending from Hagerstown, Maryland, through West Virginia and Pennsylvania, serving Pittsburgh and northeastern Ohio, and reaching Toledo. FreightWaves has reached out to W&LE management for comment. candidates.title: Project to protect rail line in San Clemente, Calif., gets Coastal Commission approval
candidates.excerpt: SAN CLEMENTE, Calif. — The Orange County Transportation Authority has received the go-ahead from the California Coastal Commission for its project to protect the LOSSAN Rail Corridor route through San Clemente. OCTA owns the former Santa Fe right-of-way along the Orange County coast used by Amtrak, Metrolink, and BNSF Railway trains. At a meeting last week, the Coastal Commission unanimously approved the OCTA’s plan calling for protection of the rail line by retaining and adding to more than 46,000 tons of large rock, or riprap, building a 1,200-foot seawall, and installing about 700 feet of tiebacks to reinforce the bluff along the track. candidates.excerpt: The Surface Transportation Board has ordered Union Pacific to make public a recording of Chief Executive Jim Vena’s remarks to a shipper conference, rejecting the railroad’s appeal in a dispute over whether he threatened customers who oppose its proposed acquisition of Norfolk Southern (NYSE: NSC). The board’s Nov. 4 decision leaves in place a ruling requiring the recording to lose its confidential designation. The dispute has raised questions about transparency in the merger review, with the regulator expressing “serious concerns” about whether Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP) had influenced stakeholder input on the proposed $85 billion transaction. The recording captures Vena’s address to the Southwest Association of Rail Shippers at its annual conference in Houston in March. Rival Canadian Pacific Kansas City sought its public release, arguing that Vena’s remarks allegedly threatening higher rates for shippers opposing the merger had chilled participation in the regulatory proceeding. candidates.title: AAR Reports Weekly Rail Traffic for the Week Ending October 31, 2026
candidates.excerpt: The Association of American Railroads (AAR) reported U.S. rail traffic for the week ending October 31, 2026. For this week, total U.S. weekly rail traffic was 514,080 carloads and intermodal units, up 3.5 percent compared with the same week last year. Total carloads for the week ending October 31 were 233,816 carloads, up 3.0 percent compared with the same week in 2025, while U.S. weekly intermodal volume was 280,264 containers and trailers, up 3.9 percent compared to 2025. Seven of the 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They included metallic ores and metals, up 3,883 carloads, to 25,059; chemicals, up 2,542 carloads, to 34,523; and motor vehicles and parts, up 1,351 carloads, to 16,268. Commodity groups that posted decreases compared with the same week in 2025 were grain, down 2,092 carloads, to 23,078; miscellaneous carloads, down 1,162 carloads, to 8,369; and coal, down 224 carloads, to 55,042.
